outcomeClusters.title: Gravity
outcomes: Describe gravity as a force that acts towards the center of mass.
Understand conceptually the proportional relationships between the force of gravity, mass, and distance between the objects.
Calculate any of the variables using the equation:

outcomeClusters.title: Inertia & Newton's First Law
outcomes: State the definition of inertial mass.
Define inertia and explain how it is related to Newton’s first law.
Apply Newton’s first law to identify the acceleration state of an object or objects given a description in words.

outcomeClusters.title: Forces & Free-Body Diagrams
outcomes: Identify the forces acting in a description of a physical situation.
Calculate the net force acting on an object along a single axis.
Create a free-body diagram for a given situation.

outcomeClusters.title: Equilibrium
outcomes: Define static and dynamic equilibrium.
Use a free-body diagram to calculate net force and determine equilibrium states.
Identify whether an object is in static or dynamic equilibrium given a description of the motion.
Identify that an object in equilibrium has zero acceleration.

outcomeClusters.title: Inclined Planes (with and without friction)
outcomes: Identify all the forces acting on a body that is on an inclined plane (with and without friction).
Calculate the net force acting on an object on an inclined plane (with and without friction).
Calculate the acceleration of an object on an inclined plane (with and without friction).

outcomeClusters.title: Newton's Second Law
outcomes: Apply Newton’s second law to a description of a problem to determine the acceleration state of the object.
Use a free-body diagram to calculate the acceleration of an object.

outcomeClusters.title: Action/Reaction Pairs (Newton's Third Law)
outcomes: Identify an action/reaction pair.
Identify an action/reaction pair as acting on two separate objects.
Contrast action/reaction pairs and balanced forces.

outcomeClusters.title: Hooke's Law & Springs
outcomes: State Hooke’s law both mathematically and conceptually.
Calculate the spring force or the spring constant given the other two variables.
Calculate the spring constant of a spring from a force-extension graph.
